Ward will stick around in Baltimore and would be a top candidate to be elevated to the main roster if the Ravens need more backfield depth. Ward last saw regular-season action in 2024 with the Steelers, when he logged five carries for 22 yards across four games.

items.headline: Bell (coach's decision) is inactive for Week 1 against the Texans.
items.summary: Bell didn't appear on the injury report at all this week, so it appears the rookie fourth-round pick will be a healthy scratch. While Bell still has a promising long-term outlook after a solid Week 3 effort in the preseason, this doesn't bode well for anyone hoping for early-season utility. In his stead, veteran Greg Dortch, who was elevated from the practice squad Saturday, will get the nod on the active roster.

items.headline: Coleman caught his lone target for one yard in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.summary: Buffalo continued to use a rotation at wide receiver to open the 2026 campaign. While DJ Moore paced the group with 26 routes on Josh Allen's 32 dropbacks, Khalil Shakir (20), Coleman (19) and Joshua Palmer (13) fell in line behind him. Between Coleman and Palmer, it was the latter who had the big play, recording what proved to be the game-winning 34-yard touchdown catch with 1:37 left in the fourth quarter. Coleman was targeted on the subsequent failed two-point conversion, and he'll likely need an injury ahead of him to have any fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Cook rushed 13 times for 57 yards and caught three of four targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 36-31 win over the Texans.
items.summary: Cook didn't find much room against Houston's stout front and took a back seat to Josh Allen, who had two rushing touchdowns and two touchdown passes. Allen's presence didn't stop Cook from rushing for a league-high 1,621 rushing yards during the 2025 regular season, so there should be better days ahead for Buffalo's shifty running back. Cook will have a short turnaround before Buffalo's home opener against the Lions on Thursday.

items.headline: Davis rushed one time for three yards in Buffalo's 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.summary: Frank Gore actually out-snapped Davis 10 to five behind James Cook, as both Davis and Gore rushed one time for three yards. If something were to ever happen to Cook, it looks like Gore could actually have a bigger role than expected, making Davis a shakier bench stash in fantasy.

items.headline: Dortch reverted to the Bills' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Dortch was elevated to the active roster for a return role with the Bills' special teams unit. The wide receiver played 10 special teams snaps, taking two punt returns for 10 yards and three kick returns for 82 yards en route to a 36-31 Bills victory. Dortch can only be elevated for two more regular-season games before he must be signed to the active roster to play for the team.

items.headline: Gore reverted to the practice squad after recording one carry for three yards in Buffalo's 36-31 win over Houston on Sunday, according to the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: The running back played on 11 offensive snaps and four special-teams snaps. Gore was elevated for Week 1 because Ty Johnson was dealing with a hamstring injury. If Johnson can play in Week 2, it seems unlikely that Gore will be elevated again.

items.headline: Hawes didn't record any offensive snaps during Buffalo's win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.summary: Hawes was in the starting lineup alongside both Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox but served mainly in a blocking capacity, as he failed to record any targets across 25 offensive snaps. The 25-year-old also saw eight snaps on special teams and should continue to see similar usage going forward unless either Kincaid or Knox is forced to miss time.

items.headline: The Bills listed Johnson (hamstring) as a limited participant on Monday's estimated practice report.
items.summary: After missing the Bills' first two practices of Week 1, Johnson returned to the field Friday as a limited participant and took a questionable tag into Sunday's season opener versus the Texans. Johnson ultimately was inactive for the 36-31 win, but he'll have a stronger chance of making his 2026 debut Thursday against the Lions if he can upgrade to full participation in practice at some point over the next two days.

items.headline: Kincaid caught five of six targets for 130 yards in Sunday's 36-31 win over the Texans.
items.summary: Kincaid did most of his damage late, recording catches of 40 and 35 yards in the fourth quarter. He cleared offseason addition DJ Moore by 30 receiving yards for the team lead while tying Khalil Shakir for second in targets behind Moore's eight. Kincaid played through a knee injury last season but looked healthy in this season opener while setting a new single-game career high in receiving yards. He'll try to keep rolling in Thursday's Week 2 home game against the Lions.

items.headline: Knox caught his only target for seven yards in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.summary: Buffalo started the game in 13 personnel, featuring all three of Dalton Kincaid, Knox and Jackson Hawes at tight end. Knox ended up playing 38 of 57 offensive snaps and blocked on 23 of those, as he ran just 12 routes overall. Knox and Hawes allow Kincaid to focus on his role as a pass catcher, and the latter ended up leading the team with a 5-130-0 receiving line on six targets.

items.headline: Shakir caught four of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 36-31 win over the Texans.
items.summary: Shakir finished a distant third on the Bills in receiving yards behind Dalton Kincaid and DJ Moore, each of whom reached the 100-yard mark. Moore paced the team with eight targets in his Bills debut, while Shakir and Kincaid tied for second with six apiece. Shakir gets most of his opportunities on short passes near the line of scrimmage, so he's likely to keep getting looks from Josh Allen after leading the team in targets each of the past two seasons, but most of the downfield opportunities should go to alternative options, thus capping Shakir's ceiling. Buffalo will play its home opener Thursday against the Lions.

items.headline: Buechele signed a practice-squad contract with Buffalo on Monday, Alec White and Mike Maynard of the team's official site report.
items.summary: Buechele spent training camp with the Bills but was released Sunday. However, he'll stick with the team as organizational depth on the practice squad. Unless Josh Allen or Kyle Allen become unavailable for any reason, Buechele isn't likely to be a regular part of Buffalo's game-day roster.

items.headline: Gosnell signed a practice-squad contract with Buffalo on Monday, Alec White and Mike Maynard of the team's official site report.
items.summary: Gosnell spent all of last season on the Bills' practice squad and will open the 2026 campaign there as well. The 24-year-old had a relatively quiet preseason, catching three of four targets for 44 yards over three games. Gosnell's chance of seeing action on game days this season likely hinges on whether injuries beset Buffalo's wideout corps.

items.headline: Maclin inked a practice-squad contract with Buffalo on Monday, Alec White and Mike Maynard of the team's official site report.
items.summary: Maclin joined the Bills as an undrafted free agent in early May and had some promising moments during the preseason slate, including a 71-yard touchdown catch. He was waived Sunday but will remain in the Buffalo organization on the practice squad. Maclin's path to game-day opportunities will likely depend upon the health of the Bills' receiver corps.

items.headline: Sherfield signed a contract to join Buffalo's practice squad Monday. Alec White and Mike Maynard of the team's official site report.
items.summary: Sherfield was released Sunday but quickly came to a deal to remain in the organization. The 30-year-old played in 12 regular-season games between Arizona and Denver last year, totaling three catches on four targets for 21 yards while also contributing on special teams. Sherfield will serve as organizational wideout depth for Buffalo and would be a prime candidate to be elevated if injuries hit the club's receiver room.

items.headline: Dillon handled five carries for 28 yards during Sunday's 59-37 loss versus the Bears.
items.summary: All of Dillon's touches came during Carolina's last drive of the game, when Chicago was leading by 22 points with less than four minutes remaining and more than content to let the Panthers run out the clock. Chuba Hubbard and 2024 second-rounder Jonathon Brooks should still probably be considered as being ahead of Dillon in line for carries going into Week 2.

items.headline: Evans caught one of two targets for nine yards in Sunday's 59-37 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Evans was on the field for 27 of the team's 68 offensive snaps while operating as the team's primary reserve option at tight end behind Tommy Tremble. Evans also logged 17 snaps with the special-teams unit, and he will continue to have limited offensive upside in Week 2 against the Falcons.

items.headline: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Panthers' emergency third quarterback against the Bears on Sunday, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
items.summary: King beat out Kyle Trask for a spot on the Panthers' 53-man roster at the conclusion of training camp, and the former will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Bryce Young and backup Kenny Pickett for Week 1. That means King will not be allowed to play Sunday unless both Young and Pickett were removed from the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Legette failed to haul in either of his targets and returned two kickoffs for 51 yards during Carolina's loss to the Bears on Sunday.
items.summary: Legette had a quiet outing despite playing 36 of the team's 68 snaps. The 2024 first-round pick will look to be more involved offensively during next week's game against the Falcons but will most likely continue to see the majority of his production come on special teams unless either Tetairoa McMillan or Jalen Coker is forced to miss time.

items.headline: Metchie (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Bears, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
items.summary: Metchie did enough in training camp to earn a spot on the Panthers' 53-man roster, though he'll observe Sunday's game in street clothes while Jimmy Horn and Brycen Tremayne serve as Carolina's rotational wide receivers behind Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. Metchie's next chance to play is Week 2 against the Falcons on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.headline: Sanders (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Sanders, a fourth-round selection of the Panthers in the 2024 NFL Draft, will be a healthy scratch for Week 1 while Carolina rolls with Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans, Darren Waller and Feleipe Franks as the active tight ends for Sunday's regular-season opener. Sanders' next chance to suit up is Week 2 against the Falcons on Sunday, Sept. 20, though he may not be active for a game unless there's an injury to a tight end ahead of him on the depth chart.

items.headline: Tremble caught three of his five targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 59-37 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Tremble played 34 offensive snaps, which ended up being just under 56 percent of the Panthers' total offensive plays. The tight end also contributed 11 special teams snaps in the losing effort, showing some versatility in what was overall a productive offensive day for the Panthers.

items.headline: Waller secured both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
items.summary: Waller actually had a one-yard touchdown called back on a penalty on the Panthers' opening drive. Carolina used all three of Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans and Waller pretty heavily against Chicago, and both Tremble and Waller each ran 18 routes. Waller isn't going to be a full-time player, but it's clear he's going to be featured in the scoring area. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet most weeks and gets a road date with the Falcons next Sunday.

items.headline: Marshall was signed to Carolina's practice squad Thursday, Darin Gantt of Panthers.com reports.
items.summary: Marshall went undrafted in 2025 but has been affiliated with the Browns ever since, mostly serving as a member of the team's practice squad. However, he didn't make Cleveland's 53-man roster and was cut Sunday. The 24-year-old most recently appeared in three preseason games for the Browns in 2026, amassing 46 yards off 23 carries while adding six catches for 48 yards and a touchdown. While Marshall still has a way to go before taking the field for a regular-season game, he will get another opportunity to remain in the league in some capacity with the Panthers' practice squad.

items.headline: The Panthers signed Moore to their practice squad Monday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Moore will stick around in Carolina, albeit on the practice squad, after previously being released by the team. The 31-year-old caught just one pass across four appearances with the Panthers last season. He will likely only be elevated should the team suffer injuries at the position.

items.headline: The Panthers signed Reed to their practice squad Monday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Reed will stick around on Carolina's practice squad after being unable to earn a spot on the active roster. The 2025 undrafted free agent spent last season on the team's practice squad as well but didn't appear in any games, and will look to make his regular-season debut during the upcoming campaign.

items.headline: The Panthers signed Tyus to their practice squad Monday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Tyus signed a reserve/future contract with Carolina but was unable to earn a roster spot. With only three running backs on the active roster and both Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) and Jonathon Brooks (general soreness) dealing with injuries, Tyus could be elevated for the team's Week 1 matchup against the Bears.

items.headline: The Panthers signed Washington to their practice squad Monday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Washington was unable to earn a roster spot with Carolina after signing with the team last month but is now set to stick around on the practice squad. The 25-year-old has caught just seven passes for 108 yards across 15 career appearances and is unlikely to contribute to the Panthers' offense even if elevated.

items.headline: Bagent (back) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
items.summary: Bagent didn't practice at all during the week, so Case Keenum will serve as the QB2 behind Caleb Williams against Carolina. Bagent logged a total of 14 offensive snaps last regular season.

items.headline: Burden caught all five of his targets for 63 yards and added two yards on his only carry in Sunday's 59-37 win over the Panthers.
items.summary: In the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history, Burden didn't make a huge impact but did the most he could with the targets he got. The Bears' running game was the engine of the offense in this one -- six of their eight TDs came on the ground -- and that balance will tip toward the pass-catchers sooner or later. Burden will look for more volume in Week 2 at home against the Vikings.

items.headline: Davis reverted to the Bears' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Davis played 10 offensive snaps for the Bears but did not appear in the box score. The wide receiver's real value came on special teams when he recovered Jimmy Horn's muffed punt to steal a possession for the Bears.

items.headline: Johnson currently is the only healthy running back on the Bears' active roster after D'Andre Swift (abdomen) exited Thursday's practice due to an injury, Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune reports.
items.summary: With Kyle Monangai still in recovery mode from a hyperextended knee, Swift was the unquestioned top healthy back in Chicago before he was seen holding at his midsection as he left the field Thursday. Following cut-down day and its aftermath, Johnson now is the lone player at the position who isn't banged up, while Salvon Ahmed is the sole RB on the practice squad. Since the Bears used a fourth-round pick on him in 2023, Johnson's role on offense has dwindled in each subsequent campaign, including just two carries and no targets in seven appearances last season.

items.headline: The Bears signed Moss to the practice squad and elevated him to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: The Bears waived Moss during cutdown day. The quarterback cleared waivers and signed back with the team's practice squad Saturday. The Bears required the QB on the practice squad so they could elevate him to the active roster ahead of Sunday's showdown with the Panthers,  where he will likely be the emergency No. 3 QB behind Caleb Williams and Case Keenum as Tyson Bagent (back) deals with an injury.

items.headline: Raymond caught eight of his nine targets for 84 yards in Sunday's 59-37 win over the Panthers.
items.summary: Raymond caught the most passes for the Bears in Week 1 while also being targeted nearly twice as much as the next closest target (Luther Burden with five). The Bears' rushing game was the star of the show, totaling 291 yards and six touchdowns, but Raymond was the centerpiece of the passing offense in Sunday's win and could maintain this level of attention in future weeks.

items.headline: The Bears placed Large (undisclosed) on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.summary: Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports general manager Ryan Poles stated the Bears will "remain flexible" on both Large and safety Coby Bryant (knee) as they manage their injuries. Large must spend at least four regular-season games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the team's 53-man roster. The status of the tight end's injury still remains unclear, so it is uncertain if he will need longer to recover.

items.headline: Chicago signed Ahmed to its practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Ahmed made a late push for a spot on the Bears' initial 53-man roster for 2026, showing off some capability as a receiver during the preseason, but he just missed the cut before being brought onto the practice squad. With that said, his status will be worth monitoring as early as Week 1 if Kyle Monangai (knee) proves unavailable to start the regular season.

items.headline: Chicago signed Carlson to its practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Bears released Carlson on Sunday, opting to keep only three healthy tight ends on their initial 53-man roster for 2026. He appeared in two regular-season games with Chicago in 2025 but did not register any targets.

items.headline: The Bears signed Ismail to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: The Bears waived Ismail during Sunday's cut-down day. The tight end cleared waivers and will return to the team's practice squad, where he spent the end of the 2026 season. Ismail has yet to suit up for an NFL regular-season game.

items.headline: Chicago signed Miller to its practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Miller was released Sunday after he failed to make the cut for the Bears' initial 53-man roster for 2026, but he's sticking around as a practice squadder. If he finds his way onto the field during the regular season, he'll likely be limited to trying to draw targets from the slot.

items.headline: Chicago signed Richardson to its practice squad Monday.
items.summary: As he did last year, Richardson will begin the regular season on the Bears' practice squad after missing the cut for their initial 53-man roster. He did dress for one game in 2025, but he's still waiting to record his first regular-season NFL snap.

items.headline: Chicago signed Scott to its practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: After spending his rookie season playing third fiddle to veteran Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason, Scott was replaced on the Vikings' depth chart by rookie sixth-rounder Demond Claiborne during training camp and cuts. His ability as a receiver could create at least a little fantasy intrigue if he finds his way onto the field with the Bears during the regular season.

items.headline: All saw 20 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Sunday's 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
items.summary: The 2024 fourth-round pick operated as the third tight end behind Drew Sample (41 snaps) and Mike Gesicki (21 snaps). All made 20 catches as a rookie two years ago before missing the 2025 campaign with a right-knee injury. He doesn't seem like much of a factor in the receiving game right now.

items.headline: Endries (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Bucs.
items.summary: The tight end is buried on the depth chart behind Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All. Endries did earn a roster spot out of training camp after getting picked in the seventh round by the Bengals back in April.

items.headline: Gesicki caught five passes on seven targets for 78 yards and a touchdown during the Bengals' 33-27 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.summary: Even with the lethal one-two punch of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, it was Gesicki who led the Bengals in catches, targets and receiving yards during Sunday's win, which included a two-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow late in the first quarter. Gesicki was also Burrow's go-to target late in the second quarter, with the duo connecting on passes of 16, 11 and 20 yards to help set up a 20-yard field goal from Evan McPherson. Chase, Higgins and running back Chase Brown are still the main playmakers on offense for the Bengals, but Gesicki is more than capable of having games like Sunday. The Bengals will look to start the 2026 season with a 2-0 record next Sunday on the road against the Texans, whose defense gave up 36 points to the Bills and allowed tight end Dalton Kincaid to turn six targets into five catches for 130 yards in Week 1.

items.headline: Hudson reverted to the Bengals' practice squad after catching one pass for four yards in Sunday's 33-27 win over the Bucs, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: The tight end played on six offensive snaps and 13 special-teams snaps. Hudson got the nod over rookie seventh-round pick Jack Endries as the fourth tight end on Cincinnati's depth chart. Endries, though, is not injured, so it's not clear which player will hold down the spot if the Bengals again carry four players at the position in their next game.

items.headline: Iosivas caught two passes on three targets for 12 yards during the Bengals' 33-27 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.summary: Iosivas played 39 of 64 snaps on offense, third-most among Bengals wide receivers behind Ja'Marr Chase (60) and Tee Higgins (46), though it was tight end Mike Gesicki's 5-78-1 receiving line that led all Cincinnati pass catchers. Iosivas is firmly entrenched as the Bengals' WR3, though he's unlikely to see many targets from Joe Burrow while Chase, Higgins, Gesicki and running back Chase Brown are on the field. Up next is a Week 2 clash against the Steelers on Sept. 27.

items.headline: Perine rushed five times for 20 yards and caught all three targets for 30 yards in a 33-27 win over Tampa Bay on Sunday.
items.summary: Perine was the only Bengals running back besides starter Chase Brown (16-56-1 rushing line) to record a carry, and he also finished with Cincinnati's third-highest receiving yardage total. Perine fell off quite a bit as a pass catcher last year, finishing with just 17 receptions for 87 yards over 15 games, so his usage in that capacity Sunday was promising in terms of his potential fantasy value. The Bengals next make a trip to Houston, and though the Texans were one of the league's best defenses last year, they gave up 409 total yards to Buffalo on Sunday.

items.headline: Sample caught all three of his targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 33-27 win versus the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Sample was on the field for 42 of Cincinnati's 64 offensive snaps in Week 1, easily pacing Bengals tight ends in playing time. He has never been a truly explosive pass-catching threat, but a sustained high catch rate and regular playing time should keep him in the mix in a crowded passing attack.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Bullock to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Bengals waived Bullock during Sunday's cut-down day. The undrafted free agent out of South Alabama cleared waivers and promptly rejoined the team that took a shot on him. Bullock will need to compete with Kendall Milton throughout the season to be the primary practice squad running back in case the 53-man roster needs a reserve due to injury.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Clifford to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Bengals waived Clifford during Sunday's cut-down day. The quarterback was able to clear waivers and has now returned to the team. Clifford will likely return to the active roster if Joe Burrow or Joe Flacco suffer an injury that requires them to miss time.

items.headline: Johnson agreed to join the Bengals' practice squad Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.summary: Cincinnati opted to keep Joe Burrow and Joe Flacco as its sole quarterbacks on the 53-man roster heading into the regular season, but Johnson -- who was with the club for training camp and the preseason -- will remain in the organization as a depth option at the position on the practice squad. The 40-year-old signal-caller has been part of 14 different NFL teams over his long career and spent all of 2025 with the Commanders, appearing in five games and completing 34 of 54 pass attempts for 372 yards and a 1:2 TD:INT to go with 55 rushing yards and a touchdown on 12 carries.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Milton to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Bengals waived Milton during Sunday's cut-down day. The running back cleared waivers and has now rejoined the team as a member of the practice squad. Milton was unable to surpass Tahj Brooks or Samaje Perine for a depth position behind Chase Brown, but if any of the rushers on the initial 53-man roster go down, Milton could see an elevation during the regular season.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Moore to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Bengals waived Moore as part of Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and has accepted a spot with the practice squad. Moore was unable to make the cut for a stacked wide receiver room, but the former Duke pass-catcher still has a chance to play in the regular season. If the 24-year-old can outperform Noah Thomas, he should be the primary option for elevation to the active roster in case of injury to the starting wide receivers.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Thomas to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Bengals waived Thomas during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and joined the practice squad as a free agent. The undrafted free agent out of Texas A&M will now compete with Jordan Moore to be the primary wide receiver option for elevation to the active roster if it becomes necessary over the course of the regular season.

items.headline: Bond (concussion) has cleared protocol and is practicing Monday, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
items.summary: Bond was concussed in Cleveland's second preseason game and was nearing 100 percent at the end of August. He's expected to fill the WR4 role for the Browns behind KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy. As a rookie last season, Bond caught just 18 of 44 targets for 338 yards and zero touchdowns as a deep threat.

items.headline: Concepcion caught four of his five targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 34-10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: While Concepcion paced the team with his five targets, he ran just 20 routes on Deshaun Watson's 30 dropbacks, good for fourth on the Browns behind Denzel Boston (30), Jerry Jeudy (25) and Harold Fannin (24). It's going to be very difficult for this lackluster Cleveland offense to support any pass catchers as every-week fantasy starters. Concepcion will be a WR4/5 for next Sunday's road date with the Bucs.

items.headline: Fannin brought in two of three targets for 21 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
items.summary: Deshaun Watson mostly struggled against an aggressive Jaguars defense that sacked him five times and picked him off once, so Fannin's generally disappointing numbers don't look quite as bleak within that context. The talented second-year tight end still is projected to remain a critical piece in the Browns' passing game, and Fannin could see a larger role as soon as a Week 2 road matchup against the Buccaneers.

items.headline: Jeudy caught two passes on four targets for 26 yards during the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
items.summary: Jeudy's first target from Deshaun Watson in the first quarter resulted in an interception, leading to a 30-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to Parker Washington. Jeudy and Watson connected on passes of 20 and six yards late in the second quarter, but the sixth-year wide receiver did not see a target in the second half. His 32 snaps on offense were third-most behind rookies Denzel Boston (47) and KC Concepcion (35), and Jeudy is also competing with tight end Harold Fannin for targets. Up next is a Week 2 road clash against the Buccaneers on Sept. 20.

items.headline: Sampson (knee) is expected to miss "significant time," Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Sampson hurt his left knee in Sunday's Week 1 loss to Jacksonville and was on crutches while wearing a brace after the game. It appears that further evaluation on the running back has concluded that Sampson is dealing with a significant injury. It's not yet clear exactly how much time he'll miss, though there certainly a chance he'll end up on IR. Raheim Sanders will likely take on a bigger role in Sampson's absence, and Jaleel McLaughlin could be summoned from the practice squad.

items.headline: Sanders caught all three of his targets for 25 yards and added one rush on the ground for a yard in Sunday's 34-10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: Sanders had an opportunity to mix into the offense after Dylan Sampson (knee) sustained an injury during the Week 1 contest. The running back played 18 of the 51 offensive snaps for the Browns while also adding 130 kick return yards on three returns. Sanders was utilized far more in the receiving game, letting Quinshon Judkins take the majority of the carries.

items.headline: The Browns signed McLaughlin to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: McLaughlin was waived by the Broncos on Sunday but will get a new opportunity with the Browns, where he would be a top candidate for elevation to the active roster if one of Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson or Raheim Sanders miss time. McLaughlin appeared in eight regular-season games for Denver last year, logging 37 carries for 187 yards and a touchdown while adding four catches on six targets for 27 yards.

items.headline: Means was signed to Browns' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Means was cut loose by the Saints on August 29 after spending the first two-plus seasons of his career with the team. The wide receiver was selected in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft by New Orleans and he spent the entirety of the 2025 campaign on injured reserve after suffering a lower-leg injury during the preseason. Means will look to prove himself with Cleveland and earn an elevation to the active roster at some point this fall.

items.headline: The Browns signed Swingson to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Swinson failed to crack the Packers' 53-man roster and was waived by the team Sunday. He'll get a fresh opportunity in Cleveland and would be a candidate for elevation to the active roster if one of Harold Fannin, Blake Whiteheart or Carsen Ryan were to miss time. Swinson has yet to play in an NFL regular-season game since entering the league in May of 2024 as an undrafted free agent.

items.headline: Wilson was signed to the Browns practice squad Monday.
items.summary: After recently being waived by Cleveland, Wilson will now be brought back as a member of the Browns' practice squad. The 22-year-old finished his final collegiate season at Baylor, where he caught 44 passes for 591 yards and five touchdowns while also playing a prominent role on special teams.

items.headline: The Cowboys signed Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: Abanikanda joined up with the Cowboys' practice squad after being waived by the team Aug. 30. The running back will now get a shot at a depth role on the active roster due to the placement of Malik Davis (hip) on IR. Javonte Williams and Emari Demercado will likely see most of the offensive action, but Abanikanda could acquire a few carries alongside a moderate special teams workload.

items.headline: Browns is one of six wide receivers on the Cowboys' initial 53-man roster, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.summary: The Cowboys seem to have found a diamond in the rough with Brown, who signed with the team as an undrafted free agent in May after recording 1,079 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns at Georgia Southern in 2025. Prior to that, Brown played at Auburn for three years. Brown's two-touchdown performance in the Cowboys' preseason opener helped him earn a spot on the team, but Ryan Flournoy remains the favorite to join CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in three-receiver sets.

items.headline: Demercado recorded two carries for seven yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Demercado operated as the team's No. 2 option at running back in Week 1 behind starter Javonte Williams, but he was limited to just five snaps on offense in the contest. Demercado signed with Dallas on Aug. 31, and his role could grow as he continues to get more comfortable in the Cowboys' offense moving forward.

items.headline: Howell is set to be the backup quarterback to Dak Prescott for the Cowboys' Week 1 game against the Giants.
items.summary: The Cowboys waived Joe Milton on Tuesday, leaving Howell as the sole reserve quarterback on the 53-man roster. The 25-year-old signed with the team in March after failing to have his contract extended by the Eagles during the 2025 season. The 2022 fifth-round pick by the Commanders will now start his second NFL contract with a division rival.

items.headline: Mingo caught his sole target for 10 yards in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Mingo played 11 of 58 offensive snaps and six special teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver seems to be getting mixed in on snaps when CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens or Ryan Flournoy need a break. Mingo remains the fifth option for the Cowboys wide receiver corps and will likely continue to see minimal opportunities in a highly competitive room.

items.headline: Pickens caught three of six targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Pickens had a couple drops in Sunday night's underwhelming season-opening performance. He was also quiet Week 1 last season with a 30-yard receiving performance against the Eagles, but Pickens went on to post career highs with 1,429 receiving yards and nine TDs during the 2025 regular season. The talented wide receiver has a nice rebound opportunity coming up Week 2 against a Washington secondary that was among the league's leakiest in 2025.

items.headline: Prescott completed 22 of 34 passes for 175 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants. He also rushed twice for 14 yards.
items.summary: Prescott connected with CeeDee Lamb for a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter and found Javonte Williams for a 17-yard touchdown in the fourth. Prescott's interception in the final minute of the first half proved costly, as the Giants scored a go-ahead touchdown six plays later and led the rest of the way. Lamb finished with just 44 yards and George Pickens had only 28, as Dallas' talented passing game was stuck in first gear. Prescott, who finished third in the league with 4,552 passing yards during the 2025 regular season, will try to pick up the pace in Dallas' Week 2 home opener against the Commanders.

items.headline: Schoonmaker finished with one catch for 12 yards in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: The tight end played on 13 of 58 offensive snaps and 10 more on special teams. Schoonmaker, now in his fourth NFL season, has 50 career catches in the regular season.

items.headline: Turpin returned five kicks for 122 yards and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Turpin only saw eight offensive snaps on the night, receiving his only catch in that small window of opportunity. What the wide receiver missed on offense, he made up for on special teams with six snaps for 122 explosive return yards that kept the Dallas offense in solid field position all evening.

items.headline: The Cowboys signed Hudson to a practice-squad contract Tuesday.
items.summary: Hudson linked up with Dallas as an undrafted free agent in early May. He performed well in preseason play, catching seven of eight targets for 120 yards and a touchdown over three games. Though Hudson was cut Sunday, he cleared waivers and will open the campaign on the Cowboys' practice squad.

items.headline: The Cowboys signed Milton to their practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Milton is staying in Dallas after going unclaimed on waivers. The 26-year-old completed 29 of  his 43 passes attempts for 378 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions across three preseason outings and will likely serve as the team's emergency third quarterback behind Dak Prescott and Sam Howell.

items.headline: Dallas signed Mitchell to its practice squad Thursday, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports.
items.summary: Mitchell cleared waivers after getting cut by the Panthers on Sunday, and he's getting an opportunity with a new team less than a week later. In a corresponding transaction, the Cowboys cut tight end Mitch Van Vooren.

items.headline: Smith inked a practice-squad contract with Dallas on Tuesday.
items.summary: Smith was selected by the Cowboys in the seventh round of April's NFL Draft. He played in all three of the team's preseason games, catching seven of 13 targets for 65 yards. Smith was waived Sunday, but he was quickly brought back to serve as wideout depth on the team's practice squad.

items.headline: Trigg signed a contract to join Dallas' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Trigg joined the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent in April and played in two preseason games, catching four of eight targets for 30 yards. He was waived Sunday but showed well enough during training camp for Dallas to want to bring him back as organizational tight-end depth on the practice squad.

items.headline: Badie (coach's decision) is inactive for Monday's game against the Chiefs, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
items.summary: Badie beat out Jaleel McLaughlin for a final spot on the Broncos' 53-man roster at the end of training camp. However, Badie will observe Monday night's contest in street clothes while the Broncos roll with three active running backs in RJ Harvey, J.K. Dobbins and rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman. Badie's next chance to suit up is Week 2 against the Jaguars this Sunday.

items.headline: Bryant is slotted in as a top reserve option on the Broncos' unofficial depth chart.
items.summary: Bryant reeled in 31 of 49 targets for 378 yards and a touchdown over 15 regular-season contests in his rookie campaign with Denver in 2025. The 23-year-old possesses a 6-foot-2, 200-plus pound frame, and he's on track to operate as the immediate backup behind Courtland Sutton as a boundary receiver with Denver this season. Bryant has already impressed with his physicality at his position, and he could earn more opportunities in his first campaign with new play caller Davis Webb.

items.headline: Coleman is likely to serve as the Broncos' between-the-tackles complement to starter J.K. Dobbins this season, Nick Kosmider of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Coleman was selected in the fourth round of April's draft after completing his four-year college career with a 2025 campaign with Washington during which he compiled 758 yards and 15 touchdowns on 156 carries over 12 contests. He also added 31 catches for 354 yards and two scores during his senior season. The Huskies played with an up-tempo style, so Coleman was on the field for all downs, resulting in him becoming a capable receiver and pass blocker. The running back is considered a more physical back than RJ Harvey, who also is set to serve as a reserve option behind Dobbins this season, and as a result, Coleman could be ticketed to serve more frequently as a direct replacement for Dobbins.

items.headline: Dobbins rushed eight times for 36 yards and wasn't targeted in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night.
items.summary: The highlight of Dobbins' relatively unremarkable night came early in the third quarter, when he changed direction shortly after taking the handoff and rumbled around left end for a 17-yard gain. The veteran back otherwise found running room difficult to come by against a dominant Chiefs defense, and Dobbins' rushing opportunities were notably limited overall due to game script. There will be much more cohesive offensive performances for the Broncos this season, and Dobbins should be in line for a bigger workload during Denver's home opener Week 2 against the Jaguars.

items.headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Broncos' emergency third quarterback against the Chiefs on Monday, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
items.summary: Jarrett Stidham will serve as the Broncos' backup behind Bo Nix this season. As the emergency third quarterback, Ehlinger is not allowed to play Monday unless both Nix and Stidham were to leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Bo Nix dots Evan Engram to put the Broncos on the board
items.summary: Bo Nix dots Evan Engram to put the Broncos on the board

items.headline: Harvey rushed three times for 18 yards, brought in all four targets for 23 yards and returned four kickoffs for 111 yards in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night.
items.summary: Harvey saw an uptick in opportunities as a pass catcher due to game script, one that saw the Broncos fall behind by a 24-10 margin late in the third quarter. The second-year back also was efficient with his trio of carries, which were five fewer than those logged by lead runner J.K. Dobbins. Harvey should have a chance for more opportunities on the ground in most games this season, including a Week 2 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday where Denver's offense will have a higher probability of running a more balanced attack.

items.headline: Mims (hip) has re-entered Monday's Week 1 matchup against the Chiefs, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
items.summary: Mims exited to the locker room in the first quarter and was deemed questionable to return by Denver. However, he returned to the sideline shortly thereafter, then came back into the contest during a punt return. Mims should thus be good to go for the remainder of the matchup unless he aggravates the issue or suffers another injury.

items.headline: Coach Sean Payton said Wednesday that Stidham will be the Broncos' backup quarterback to begin the 2026 season, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.summary: Sam Ehlinger pushed Stidham during training camp for his spot on Denver's depth chart behind starter Bo Nix, and the team opted to keep three quarterbacks on its initial 53-man roster, but at least for now, Stidham is second in the pecking order. Unless Nix gets hurt at some point, neither Stidham nor Ehlinger would be expected to get any snaps in a reasonably close game.

items.headline: Sutton secured two of five targets for 11 yards in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night.
items.summary: Sutton, along with the rest of the Broncos offense, endured a miserable night, and the veteran receiver tied for the second-fewest receptions and third-fewest yards among Denver pass catchers to record at least one grab. Sutton also was the intended receiver on Bo Nix's early-game interception, making it an all-around throwaway season-opening performance. Sutton's first chance to atone comes in Denver's Week 2 home opener Sunday, which sees a talented Jaguars team come into the Mile High City.

items.headline: Waddle brought in one of three targets for two yards in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night.
items.summary: Waddle's regular-season Broncos debut was as miserable as his final line suggests, as the prominent offseason addition finished last in receptions and yards among Denver players that recorded at least one catch. One of the two targets Waddle couldn't corral was a key third-down drop early in the third quarter, although he was hardly the only underwhelming component of a pass-catching corps that produced a modest 131 total receiving yards. More productive performances are surely ahead for Waddle and the Broncos' air attack, with the first opportunity for atonement coming in a Week 2 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday.

items.headline: The Broncos signed Bandy to the practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Bandy was waived by Denver on Sunday after he failed to make the team's 53-man roster following the conclusion of training camp. However, the San Diego product impressed the coaching staff enough to stick around on the Broncos' practice squad. Marvin Mims is dealing with a foot injury, and if that issue lingers, then Bandy would be a candidate to be elevated to the Broncos' active roster for the team's regular-season opener against the Chiefs on Monday, Sept. 14.

items.headline: The Broncos signed Katsis to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Katsis didn't make the 53-man roster for the Broncos but will stay in Denver as a member of the practice squad. The 24-year-old went undrafted in 2026 after spending two collegiate seasons at Northern Arizona, where he most recently finished the 2025 campaign by amassing 60 catches for 1,016 yards and 10 touchdowns, adding five carries for 109 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: The Broncos signed Key to the practice squad Monday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Key was waived by the Broncos on Sunday, but he impressed the coaching staff enough in training camp to be invited to stay as a member of the team's practice squad. He played in all three of the Broncos' preseason games, finishing with three catches (on six targets) for 52 yards while adding a tackle on special teams.

items.headline: The Broncos signed Krull to the practice squad Monday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Krull was unable to beat Dallen Bentley for the fourth tight end spot on the Broncos' 53-man roster, resulting in the former being released Sunday. Krull will stay in Denver on the practice squad and would be a candidate for elevation to the active roster if the Broncos needed game-day depth at tight end. Krull was limited to three regular-season games last year due to a foot injury, finishing with two catches (on four targets) for 15 yards while also contributing on special teams.

items.headline: Schrader signed with the Broncos' practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Schrader put together a solid preseason with the Broncos, finishing with 24 carries for 74 yards and nine catches on as many targets for 101 yards and a touchdown across three games. It wasn't quite enough for him to crack the team's 53-man roster, but he impressed the coaching staff enough to be invited to stay in Denver on the practice squad.

items.headline: The Lions signed Conklin on Tuesday.
items.summary: Conklin failed to make the 53-man roster over the weekend but is quickly back with the team in a series of moves. The 31-year-old Conklin caught seven passes for 101 scoreless yards across 13 regular-season games with the Chargers last season and will serve as depth behind Sam LaPorta and Brock Wright with the Lions.

items.headline: The Lions signed Kennedy from their practice squad to their active roster Thursday.
items.summary: Kennedy initially missed the cut for Detroit's 53-man roster for 2026, but he's now back in the fold with Week 1 looming. He could be tasked with punt-return duties Sunday versus the Saints.

items.headline: LaPorta caught five of eight targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints.
items.summary: The tight end finished second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards on the day while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. Back trouble limited LaPorta to just nine games in 2025, but his pace during those games would have resulted in a career-high 924 receiving yards, so staying healthy will be key to his fortunes this season. LaPorta will look to make a bigger impact in Week 2 on the road against the Bills.

items.headline: Martin is the fourth and final wide receiver on the Lions' 53-man active roster for the regular season, Tim Twentyman of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Martin is slotted behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa on the wide receiver depth chart, with Kendrick Law (knee) on season-ending injured reserve. The Lions could elevate Tom Kennedy or Lucky Jackson from the practice squad to the active roster for game day. However, for now, Martin is in line to operate in an elevated role in Detroit's offense, especially if one of Brown, Williams or TeSlaa were to miss time.

items.headline: Saylors made one tackle and returned two kicks for 25 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win against the Saints.
items.summary: Saylors saw no offensive snaps in Sunday's contest, taking all 24 of his reps with the special teams unit. Saylors made one tackle on kick coverage and had two short returns in the game, taking on most of the grunt work as the Lions' offense burned bright without him.

items.headline: TeSlaa failed to haul in his only target during Detroit's overtime win over the Saints on Sunday.
items.summary: TesLaa played 55 of the team's 77 offensive snaps but was still the only Lions player who didn't record any receptions, among those who were targeted. The 2025 third-round pick had a promising rookie campaign, catching 16 passes for 239 yards and six touchdowns despite limited usage, however he is coming off a disappointing training camp. TesLaaa will look to improve upon his performance during the Week 2 matchup against the Bills.

items.headline: Vaki turned two carries into seven yards while also reeling in his only target for 11 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win against New Orleans.
items.summary: Vaki operated as the Lions' No. 2 option running back in Week 1 behind starter Jahmyr Gibbs, but he didn't really have much of an impact over his 22 offensive snaps. The running back also logged 24 snaps on special teams in the victory. Gibbs will likely continue to dominant the touches in the backfield while Isiah Pacheco (back) is on injured reserve, leaving Vaki as an unappealing fantasy option.

items.headline: Williams gathered in just four of nine targets for 45 yards during Sunday's 31-30 overtime win against the Saints.
items.summary: QB Jared Goff and Williams weren't on the same page often Week 1, as the fifth-year wide receiver's catch rate fell below 50 percent, and nearly half of Williams' yards (22) occurred on one reception. Williams is coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard campaigns, a span in which he averaged 17.2 yards per grab, so he's a good bet to bounce back in the near future, and perhaps as soon as Thursday's road showdown with the Bills.

items.headline: The Lions signed Altmyer to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Altmyer appeared in three preseason games for the Lions in 2026, throwing for 271 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions off 29-for-46 passing. While he didn't play the best throughout the preseason, he still did enough to earn a spot on Detroit's practice squad.

items.headline: Detroit signed Gordon to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Gordon didn't make the Lions' 53-man roster, though he will stick around as a member of the practice squad. The 25-year-old spent four collegiate seasons at Northwestern, totaling 54 receptions for 529 yards and two touchdowns. After spending some time with the Bears' practice squad last season, Gordon will continue his pursuit of earning a spot on an NFL roster.

items.headline: The Lions signed Jackson to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Jackson was signed by the Lions in mid-June and played well in the team's preseason finale against the Colts on Friday, when he caught five passes on as many targets for 94 yards. He didn't crack the 53-man roster and was waived by Detroit on Sunday, but he performed well enough in training camp and preseason games to be invited back by the Lions on the practice squad. Jackson last saw regular-season action in 2023 with the Vikings, when he mostly played on special teams across three regular-season games.

items.headline: The Lions signed Lovett to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Lovett was waived by the Lions on Sunday after failing to make the team's 53-man roster at the end of training camp. However, he'll take the spot on the Lions' practice squad vacated by Tyler Conklin, who signed to the team's active roster after Isiah Pacheco (back) was placed on injured reserve. Detroit has only four wide receivers on the 53-man roster, so Lovett could see some regular-season action if the Lions need more depth at the position on game day.

items.headline: Small signed to the Lions' practice squad Monday, Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press reports.
items.summary: The running back ended the 2025 campaign on Detroit's practice squad, signed a reserve/future contract with the team in January, made the initial 53-man roster out of training camp this year and then got waived Sept. 2. Small did suffer a concussion during the Lions' final preseason game, but he was let go without an injury designation or settlement, freeing him up to sign with Detroit once he cleared waivers. The former Tennessee Volunteer has yet to appear in an NFL regular-season game since coming out of college in 2024.

items.headline: Brooks turned seven carries into 29 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the Packers' 39-22 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: With Josh Jacobs (personal) on the Commissioner's Exempt List to open the season, the Packers went with a one-two punch of Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd in the backfield. Brooks 38 snaps on offense were ahead of Lloyd (30), though the latter led all Packers running backs with 13 for 37 yards. Neither RB managed to get anything going in the passing game, so the Packers may just ride the hot hand on a game-to-game basis while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers will stay on the road for their Week 2 matchup against the Jets on Sept. 20.

items.headline: Golden caught six of 12 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
items.summary: With the Packers chasing the Vikings on the scoreboard much of the fourth quarter and getting virtually nothing from their running game all day, Jordan Love dropped back to pass 46 times, and Golden's 40 routes and 12 targets both led the team, as he lined up out wide 92.5 percent of the time. The second-year wideout's 28.6 percent target share is a great sign for his fantasy viability moving forward. Golden will be a WR3 with upside next Sunday on the road against the Jets.

items.headline: The Packers signed Melton to the active roster Monday.
items.summary: Melton was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster for Sunday's loss to the Vikings. The wide receiver played 27 total snaps, catching his sole target for 10 yards on one of his seven offensive plays. The wide receiver played in 16 regular-season games for the Packers in 2025, logging four receptions for 107 yards and a touchdown as well as five rushing attempts for 35 yards.

items.headline: Moore failed to catch his only target and returned two punts for 17 yards during Green Bay's loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: Moore saw the majority of his playing time on special teams, seeing 11 snaps compared to only four on offense. The 2022 second-round pick will likely continue to serve as the team's primary returner going forward while seeing limited action on offense.

items.headline: Reed caught three of his seven targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
items.summary: Reed saw the third-most targets for the Packers behind Matthew Golden (12) and Christian Watson (eight), but the wide receiver could not haul in enough to match either's production. Tucker Kraft's 60 yards and Jonnu Smith's 50 yards also outproduced Reed on fewer targets, meaning Week 1 may not have instilled Jordan Love with much trust in the wide receiver.

items.headline: Sturdivant (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
items.summary: The undrafted rookie out of Florida impressed the Packers' coaching staff enough to crack the 53-man roster at the end of training camp, but he'll have to wait until Week 2 against the Jets on Sunday, Sept. 20, to make his regular-season debut. Bo Melton and Skyy Moore will be the depth wideouts for Sunday's NFC North clash behind Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden.

items.headline: Whyle (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Vikings.
items.summary: Whyle exited the second half of Sunday's contest with an all-too-familiar injury. The tight end missed some time in August with a minor neck issue so the current issue could be related. If Whyle is unable to return to the game, Mark Redman will likely take over as the No. 3 Packers tight end.

items.headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said Tuesday that he's "really hopeful" Musgrave (neck) will be able to play at some point during the 2026 season, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
items.summary: Green Bay placed Musgrave on the PUP list Sunday, ensuring that he'll miss at least the first four contests of the campaign. Musgrave is far from a lock to be activated when first eligible to play Week 5, as he was unable to practice at any point in training camp or the preseason after injuring his neck during June minicamp. Perhaps in part due to Musgrave's hazy return timeline in addition to the thin depth behind top tight end Tucker Kraft (knee), the Packers signed veteran Jonnu Smith to a one-year deal last week to bolster the position group.

items.headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said Tuesday that Williams is recovering from a high-ankle sprain and should be ready to return from injured reserve when first eligible Week 5, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Williams wasn't known to have sustained an injury during training camp or the preseason before he landed on injured reserve Sunday, but Gutekunst's comments provided some clarity on the matter. Assuming that the second-year wideout bounces back from the high-ankle sprain as anticipated, he should be ready to make his 2026 debut Oct. 11 versus the Bears. With Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden locked in as Green Bay's top three receivers, Williams is unlikely to run many routes when all of those players are fully healthy, but he could have a small role on offense as a gadget player in addition to serving as the team's top kickoff returner.

items.headline: The Packers signed Bankston to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Bankston was waived by the Giants on Aug. 29 but will now get another opportunity with the Packers, albeit as a member of the practice squad. The 23-year-old capped off his final collegiate season by amassing 635 yards and five touchdowns off 114 carries, adding 31 catches for 397 yards and three touchdowns in 13 games at New Mexico in 2025.

items.headline: The Packers signed Dabney to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Packers waived Dabney during Sunday's cut-down day. The tight end cleared waivers and is set to reprise his 2025 role for the organization. The 2024 undrafted free agent out of TCU joined up with the Packers' practice squad in November and will likely spend all of the 2026 season on the unit as well. Dabney was elevated for two games during the 2025 regular season, catching one pass for three yards.

items.headline: The Packers signed Hilton to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Packers waived Hilton during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and has chosen to rejoin the Packers who claimed him off waivers from the Commanders. Hilton is an undrafted free agent out of LSU and will have to fight with practice squad veterans for a chance to be elevated to the active roster at some point during the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: The Packers signed Neyor to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Packers waived Neyor during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and is once again set to spend the season on the team's practice squad. Neyor was elevated for the team's 2025 wild-card matchup against the Bears, seeing three offensive snaps in the contest.

items.headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said Tuesday that Slovis will be signed to the practice squad, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Though Slovis wasn't able to win a spot on the Cardinals' season-opening roster, the third-year quarterback made a strong impression on the Green Bay staff during the preseason finale between the two teams this past Friday. In the Cardinals' 42-38 loss, Slovis completed 21 of 35 passes for 223 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while adding 12 yards on two carries. He'll slot third on the Packers' organizational depth chart, putting him first in line to be elevated to the roster if starter Jordan Love or top backup Tyrod Taylor miss time at any point.

items.headline: Strong, who is on Green Bay's practice squad, is currently managing a hamstring issue, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
items.summary: Strong had been a candidate to be elevated for the Packers' season opener Sunday versus Minnesota since Josh Jacobs is on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but that's presumably no longer in play. It's not clear how severe Strong's injury is, and given that Jacobs could be out multiple games, Strong could still be a gameday practice-squad elevation down the line once he gets healthy.

items.headline: Boutte caught one of two targets for 21 yards in the Texans' 36-31 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
items.summary: Acquired from the Patriots toward the end of training camp, Boutte is still in the process of building rapport with C.J. Stroud while learning the playbook. Boutte played behind both Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson against Buffalo, seeing just under 46 percent of the offensive snaps. Boutte's role could grow as the season goes along, but Hutchinson has long been a favorite of the coaching staff, and second-year WR Jaylin Noel also is in the mix for increased reps.

items.headline: Brooks (hand) was not listed on Houston's official injury report Wednesday.
items.summary: Brooks broke his hand during a practice back in early August, but it doesn't look like it's holding him back anymore. He's not likely to see many snaps on offense in Week 1, barring an injury to David Montgomery or Woody Marks.

items.headline: Collins caught seven of 10 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown while adding a seven-yard run in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: C.J. Stroud connected with Collins for a 12-yard touchdown in the second quarter, marking the first touchdown of the season for both Houston's quarterback and the team's star wide receiver. Collins led the Texans in targets, catches and receiving yards Sunday after finishing as Houston's receiving yards leader in each of the previous three regular seasons. He is locked in as Stroud's top target heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals.

items.headline: Hutchinson caught three passes on six targets for 32 yards during the Texans' 36-31 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
items.summary: Hutchinson finished third among Texans pass catchers in both targets and receptions, including a 20-yard catch late in the fourth quarter. His 44 snaps on offense were second-most among wide receivers behind Nico Collins (57), suggesting that Hutchinson is the Texans' WR2 ahead of Kayshoun Boutte (36 snaps) and Jaylin Noel (24 snaps) in the absence of Jayden Higgins (knee, IR). The Texans will stay at home for Week 2 against the Bengals on Sept. 20.

items.headline: Jordan (knee) was not listed on Houston's official injury report Wednesday.
items.summary: Jordan dealt with a knee issue during training camp and the preseason, but he's on track to be available for Week 1 versus the Bills. How much playing time he'll actually see is another question, as the Texans have four other healthy tight ends on their current 53-man roster.

items.headline: Marks rushed nine times for 42 yards and caught his lone target for a two-yard loss in the Texans' 36-31 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
items.summary: While David Montgomery stole the headlines with three total touchdowns, Montgomery wasn't exactly efficient with his 20 carries, turning them into just 60 yards (3.0 YPC). Marks averaged 4.7 yards per carry with his nine attempts and actually out-snapped his veteran backfield mate 40 to 39 and ran 20 routes to Montgomery's 14, proving the 50-50 split talk from the summer to be true in the season opener. Marks remains an elite fantasy bench stash with some standalone value as an RB3 during bye weeks.

items.headline: Noel recorded two catches for 53 yards and three kickoff returns for 70 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: The wide receiver played on 24 of 79 offensive snaps and six more on special teams. Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte all played on more offensive snaps for the Texans. Noel, though, seems secure in his role as kick and punt returner, as he also had a fair catch on a punt during the defeat.

items.headline: Schultz caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: Schultz's eight targets were second on the team to Nico Collins' 10 on 38 pass attempts by C.J. Stroud. Schultz doesn't offer much big-play ability at 30 years old, but he's a reliable target in the middle of the field and saw his floor raise when Jayden Higgins went down with a season-ending torn ACL over the summer. The veteran tight end will be a borderline TE1/2 next Sunday against the Bengals.

items.headline: Dell (knee) agreed to take a pay cut from the Texans on Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Entering the final year of his rookie deal, Dell was scheduled to collect $3.624 million, but he'll now make just over $1.7 million in 2026. Dell missed the entirety of the 2025 campaign after a catastrophic knee injury suffered toward the end of the previous season. He's now opening this season on injured reserve and won't be eligible to play until Week 5 at the earliest.

items.headline: The Texans signed Bond to their practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The rookie sixth-round pick out of Boston College was unable to secure a spot on the Texans' 53-man roster coming out of training camp, but after clearing waivers, he'll end up sticking around in the organization. The Texans have also added fellow receivers Mitchell Tinsley, Josh Kelly and Daniel Sobkowicz on the practice squad, so Bond may not necessarily rank as the top choice to get elevated to the roster if Houston requires another wideout in any given week.

items.headline: Houston is signing Gronowski to its practice squad, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Gronowski  initially signed with Miami as an undrafted free agent in May. He was cut in mid-August, then re-signed, then cut again all within the same month. Gronowski ultimately signed with the Dolphins' practice squad, but he was cut once more last Tuesday. He'll now get a chance to impress as part of the Texans' practice squad, though the organization is relatively set at QB on the active roster with C.J. Stroud and Davis Mills.

items.headline: The Texans signed Jordan to their practice squad Monday.
items.summary: A sixth-round pick in 2024, Jordan has spent his entire three-year career in the Texans organization, despite having been waived on three occasions. He spent most of his first two seasons on the practice squad and didn't make his NFL debut until Week 15 of the 2025 campaign, when he ran for 101 yards on 15 carries and added two receptions for 17 yards in a win over the Cardinals. Jordan received playing time in the remaining three contests of the regular season, churning out 92 yards on 28 carries to go with five catches for 17 yards, but he went unused during the Texans' two-game playoff run. After he was unable to win a spot on the roster coming out of the preseason, Jordan will likely rank as the Texans' top choice to receive a promotion from the practice squad if David Montgomery or Woody Marks miss time at any point in 2026.

items.headline: The Texans signed Kelly to their practice squad Monday.
items.summary: A second-year wideout from Texas Tech, Kelly is still waiting to make his NFL debut. After joining Houston on a reserve/future contract in January, Kelly was unable to make enough of an impression during training camp and the preseason to secure a spot on the roster, but the Texans will keep him around in the organization as a member of the practice squad.

items.headline: Houston signed Mitchell-Paden to its practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Mitchell-Paden cleared waivers after missing the cut for the Saints' initial 53-man roster, but now he's getting a fresh opportunity with the Texans. Barring injury to one of the five tight ends on Houston's current depth chart, there's little chance he'll see regular-season action any time soon.

items.headline: The Texans signed Sobkowicz to their practice squad Monday.
items.summary: An undrafted rookie wideouts out of Illinois State, Sobkowicz faced long odds to make the Texans' Week 1 roster, but he at least showed enough during training camp and the preseason to stick around through final roster cutdowns. After going unclaimed off waivers, Sobkowicz has elected to stick around in the Texans' organization as one of four receivers on the practice squad.

items.headline: The Texans signed Whittington to their practice squad Monday.
items.summary: After signing with the Texans in May as an undrafted rookie out of Oregon, Whittington took part in training camp and the preseason, but was unable to secure a spot on the final roster heading into Week 1. Though Whittington will stick around in the organization, Jawhar Jordan will likely rank as the Texans' preferred choice to elevate to the roster if the team's depth in the backfield gets tested at any point.

items.headline: Downs caught two of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens.
items.summary: Downs' four targets tied Jonathan Taylor for fourth on the team behind Alec Pierce (six), Keenan Allen (six) and Tyler Warren (five), but it was notable that Downs led the team with 32 routes on Daniel Jones' 34 dropbacks. He was in the slot 78.8 percent of the time, and his 93.8 percent route participation suggests Downs is an every-down wideout this season after playing behind both Michael Pittman and Pierce in previous seasons. Downs should have better days moving forward and gets a Week 2 date with the Chiefs next Sunday.

items.headline: Giddens (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.summary: Giddens missed a big chunk of training camp and the preseason due to a hamstring injury, and he was passed on the depth chart by rookie Seth McGowan as the RB2 behind workhorse back Jonathan Taylor.

items.headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive as the Colts' emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.summary: Leonard lost out on the QB2 job to Anthony Richardson behind Daniel Jones over the summer. Across five regular-season appearances last season, Leonard completed just 58.2 percent of his 67 pass attempts for 415 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions, averaging a subpar 6.2 yards per attempt.

items.headline: McGowan caught his only target for no gain and notched 164 yards on five kick returns during Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens.
items.summary: McGowan was only on the field for six of the team's 54 offensive snaps while operating as the top reserve option at running back behind Jonathan Taylor. McGowan definitely made his mark on special teams during the contest, but as long as Taylor is healthy, he will likely have a limited impact on offense.

items.headline: Ogletree (neck) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
items.summary: The tight end was limited by a neck injury a day earlier. Ogletree is trending toward playing in Sunday's opener against Baltimore. The 2022 sixth-round pick has added depth to the Colts' tight-end spot throughout his career, seeing action on special teams as well.

items.headline: Colts WR Allen relinquishes No. 13 to teammate Treadwell
items.summary: Receiver Keenan Allen will wear No. 10 with the Colts this season, marking the first time in his 13-year NFL career that he will not be wearing No. 13, which will be worn by Laquon Treadwell.

items.headline: The Colts cut Bentley from the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Bentley signed to the Colts' practice squad Monday after being waived by the team Sunday following the conclusion of training camp. He's been let go by the team for the second time in three days and will look to join an organization in need of backfield depth.

items.headline: The Colts signed Booth to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Booth failed to make the Browns' 53-man roster at the end of training camp, but he'll get a new opportunity with the Colts as a member of the team's practice squad. Across three preseason games with Cleveland, Booth turned 17 carries into 109 yards and a touchdown while adding three catches (on four targets) for minus-three yards and two kickoff returns for 54 yards.

items.headline: Brown was signed to the Colts practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Brown didn't make the Colts' 53-man roster but will at least remain with the team as a member of the practice squad. The 32-year-old has an extensive NFL resume, suiting up for the Browns, Texans, Patriots, Seahawks and Cardinals throughout his career and catching 74 passes for 752 yards and three touchdowns across 92 regular-season games.

items.headline: The Colts signed Castle to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The undrafted rookie out of Duke failed to make the Colts' 53-man roster but did enough to receive an invitation to the team's practice squad. He logged 18 carries for 88 yards across the Colts' three preseason games and would be a candidate for elevation to the active roster if one of Jonathan Taylor, Seth McGowan or DJ Giddens were to miss time.

items.headline: Fletcher was signed to the Colts' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Fletcher was cut by the Buccaneers on Aug. 29 after signing with the team as an undrafted free agent in May. The tight end will now have an opportunity to operate as an extreme depth option behind Tyler Warren with Indianapolis.

items.headline: The Colts signed Gould (groin) to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Gould appeared in 19 regular-season games for the Colts since the team drafted him in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. While the 25-year-old is on the practice squad for now, his versatility could earn him more opportunities moving forward.

items.headline: Abdullah earned a spot on the Jaguars' 53-man roster following a strong training camp, John Oehser of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Abdullah and LeQuint Allen (undisclosed) will enter the regular season as the rotational running backs behind co-starters Bhayshul Tuten (illness) and Chris Rodriguez. Abdullah played in only one of the Jaguars' three preseason games, but he did enough during training camp and joint practices to crack the 53-man roster for the 2026 campaign. The 2015 second-rounder appeared in 13 regular-season games for the Colts last year, finishing with 14 carries for 60 yards and a touchdown along with 16 catches (on 17 targets) for 99 yards.

items.headline: Allen played one offensive snap and didn't show up in the box score otherwise during Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
items.summary: The 2025 seventh-rounder was cleared to play Week 1 after being limited by a hip injury, but he was an afterthought in the Jaguars' backfield behind Bhayshul Tuten (28 snaps), Chris Rodriguez (23) and Ameer Abdullah (five). Perhaps the hip was still an issue for Allen, but he's unlikely to see much playing time on offense unless Tuten or Rodriguez were to miss time.

items.headline: Boerkircher caught his only target for nine yards during Sunday's 34-10 win versus the Browns.
items.summary: Boerkircher played 38 of Jacksonville's 57 offensive snaps in his pro debut, good for second-most among Jaguars tight ends behind Brenton Strange (39). Boerkircher was billed as more of a blocker than a route-runner when he was taken in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and at least in the short term, Strange should be expected to continue to see more targets between the two of them.

items.headline: Ewers (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
items.summary: The Jaguars traded for Ewers toward the tail end of training camp, but the 2025 seventh-rounder will be a healthy scratch Week 1 while Nick Mullens serves as Jacksonville's backup QB behind Trevor Lawrence. Ewers isn't listed as the emergency third quarterback against Cleveland, so his next chance to suit up is Week 2 against Denver on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.headline: Koziol (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
items.summary: Koziol, the Jaguars' fifth-round pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, will be a healthy inactive for Week 1, so his next chance to make his regular-season debut is Week 2 against the Broncos on Sunday, Sept. 20. Brenton Strange, Quintin Morris and rookie second-rounder Nate Boerkircher will be Jacksonville's active tight ends against Cleveland.

items.headline: Mullens reverted to the Jaguars' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
