The rookie second-round pick thus will miss at least the first four games of the campaign, allowing Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins to handle the TE reps that don't go to No. 1 option Dallas Goedert.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Gipson to the practice squad Friday.
items.summary: The move corresponds with the Eagles placing Danny Gray (undisclosed) on the practice squad injured list. Gipson spent time with the Eagles, Giants and Jets during the 2025 regular season, logging two catches for six yards, 319 yards on 12 kickoff returns and 86 yards on eight punt returns across seven games. Gipson's chances of being promoted to the active roster would increase if the Eagles needed another returner on game day.

items.headline: The Eagles placed Gray (undisclosed) on the practice squad injured list Friday.
items.summary: It's unclear what type of injury Gray is working through, nor when he picked it up, but his placement on the injured list means he is not eligible to be called up to the active roster for at least four games. The Eagles signed Xavier Gipson to the practice squad in a corresponding move.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Pierce to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Eagles released Pierce on Sunday, and the running back was immediately welcomed onto the team's practice squad. Pierce spent four years with the Texans before shifting to the Chiefs for the 2025 season. The 26-year-old played one game during the 2025 regular season, rushing four times for 10 yards.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Steele to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Eagles waived Steele last Saturday. The running back was able to clear waivers and was invited back to the team's practice squad as a free agent. Steele played in all three preseason games for the Eagles, logging 21 rush attempts for 58 yards as well as 14 receptions for 136 yards and two touchdowns. The 23-year-old will contribute to the practice squad as a reserve running back with dual-threat upside.

items.headline: Allar (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
items.summary: The Steelers opted to carry four quarterbacks on the 53-man active roster. Allar will observe Sunday's regular-season opener in street clothes while Will Howard (coach's decision) serves as Pittsburgh's emergency third quarterback behind starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph. Allar figures to be a healthy scratch for most, if not all, games this season unless one of Rodgers, Rudolph or Howard were to miss time.

items.headline: Bernard played three of Pittsburgh's 67 offensive snaps during Sunday's 20-13 win versus the Falcons.
items.summary: Bernard was able to make his pro debut in Week 1, but it didn't result in any production in the box score. Only DK Metcalf (60), Michael Pittman (56) and 2024 third-rounder Roman Wilson (35) saw any snaps at wide receiver for the Steelers on Sunday otherwise.

items.headline: Dowdle rushed eight times for 15 yards and brought in two of five targets for six yards in the Steelers' 20-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
items.summary: Dowdle trailed backfield mate Jaylen Warren by only two carries and a sole target, but he was outgained in total scrimmage yards by a 73-21 margin. Dowdle is virtually certain to have better days on the ground this season, yet Warren's efficient performance as both a runner and receiver served as a reminder of his value to the offense. Consequently, Dowdle could continue narrowly trailing his teammate in overall opportunity during a Week 2 road matchup against the Patriots next Sunday.

items.headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency third quarterback against the Falcons on Sunday.
items.summary: The Steelers opted to carry four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster. For Week 1, Howard will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph, and rookie third-rounder Drew Allar (coach's decision) will be inactive. As the emergency third quarterback, Howard is prohibited from playing in Sunday's game unless both Rodgers and Rudolph were to be removed due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Metcalf secured four of 10 targets for 40 yards in the Steelers' 20-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
items.summary: Metcalf's target total led the Steelers by a fairly comfortable margin, but the talented receiver brought in less than half of them and finished behind both Michael Pittman and Pat Freiermuth in receiving yards. The amount of attention Metcalf drew from Aaron Rodgers was nevertheless encouraging, and the valuable experience the duo garnered from working together all of last season could pay big dividends in 2026. A Week 2 road matchup against the Patriots will present less than ideal circumstances, however, as Metcalf is likely to draw plenty of coverage from shutdown cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

items.headline: Pittman caught all three of his targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Falcons.
items.summary: While Pittman was sixth on the team with three targets, seeing just a 7.5 percent target share on Aaron Rodgers' 40 throws, the newest Steelers wideout paced the team with his 58 yards. Rodgers dropped back to pass 42 times against Atlanta, and Pittman's 39 routes were second on the team behind DK Metcalf's 42. Pittman's ability closer to the line of scrimmage as a possession wideout aligns better with Rodgers, who likes to work the ball out quickly. Pittman will have a tough date with the Patriots next Sunday.

items.headline: Skowronek (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.summary: Skowronek was placed in concussion protocol at the end of August after the wide receiver suffered a head injury in the Steelers' 28-27 preseason loss to the Bills. The 29-year-old progressed through the entirety of the league's five-step protocol and was cleared by an independent neurologist before Wednesday's first official practice.

items.headline: Warren rushed 10 times for 46 yards and brought in five of six targets for 27 yards in the Steelers' 20-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: Sunday offered the first look at the division of labor between Warren and new backfield mate Rico Dowdle, and by game's end, the former had outpaced the latter by two carries and one target. Warren was by far the more efficient of the two while averaging 4.6 yards per carry to Dowdle's 1.9, and he also was the more effective receiver. Warren's lost fumble was the one blemish on his day, as it was recovered at the Steelers' 25-yard line and led to the Falcons' sole touchdown. Warren should have a solid chance of remaining the narrow leader of the ground attack in a Week 2 road showdown against the Patriots next Sunday.

items.headline: Washington caught both of his targets for 18 yards during the Steelers' 20-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
items.summary: Washington was listed as a co-starter alongside Pat Freiermuth on Sunday, though the former didn't see a target from Aaron Rodgers until the second half. Freiermuth led all Steelers tight ends with 49 snaps on offense, though Washington wasn't far behind (43) and figures to be regularly involved in 12-man personnel sets. The Steelers hit the road for a Week 2 clash against the Patriots on Sept. 20.

items.headline: Wilson grabbed three passes for 26 yards and no touchdowns in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Falcons.
items.summary: The wide receiver saw six targets in total and played on 37 of 67 offensive snaps. Wilson tied with Jaylen Warren for the second-most targets on the team behind DK Metcalf, so he's clearly a part of the passing game. What he will do with that role moving forward remains to be seen.

items.headline: The Steelers signed Homer to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Steelers released Homer during Sunday's cut-down day. Homer was quickly invited back to the team's practice squad due to a strong training camp. The running back played 10 regular-season games for the Bears in 2025, rushing once for a two-yard loss while also participating in 163 special teams snaps.

items.headline: The Steelers signed Hurleman to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Steelers waived Hurleman during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and will once again sign with the practice squad. Hurleman spent the entirety of the 2025 season on the Steelers' practice squad but did not participate in any regular-season games.

items.headline: The Steelers signed Johnson to the practice squad Tuesday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Raiders released Johnson during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver was dropped by the Steelers in early June but will return to the franchise's practice squad for the regular season. Johnson played in three regular-season games for the Steelers in 2025, catching one pass for nine yards.

items.headline: The Steelers signed McRee to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Steelers waived McRee during Sunday's cut-down day. The undrafted free agent out of USC played well enough throughout training camp to receive an invitation to the team's practice squad. McRee participated in all three preseason games, catching five of his nine targets for 60 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: The Steelers signed Nichols to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Steelers waived Nichols during Sunday's cutdown day. The running back cleared waivers and chose to accept his invitation to the team's practice squad. The 25-year-old participated in all three preseason games, rushing 20 times for 87 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: The Steelers signed Smith to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Steelers waived Smith on Sunday, and he cleared waivers and has rejoined the Steelers on the practice squad. The 27-year-old participated in the first and last preseason games for the team, catching four of his five targets for 17 yards.

items.headline: Cowing returned two punts for 17 yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams in Week 1.
items.summary: Cowing also saw five snaps on offense but wasn't' targeted by Brock Purdy. With De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) injured against the Rams and Ricky Pearsall (knee) out for the season, Cowing is looking like the Niners' current WR4 behind Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson.

items.headline: Farrell secured both of his targets for 19 yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams in Week 1.
items.summary: With George Kittle still working his way into game shape off last season's torn Achilles and Jake Tonges going down with a knee injury in the second quarter, Farrell ended up playing 46 of 65 offensive snaps and ran 19 pass routes to Kittle's 17. With Tonges looking at an extended absence, Farrell is going to see more action as the TE2.

items.headline: Hodge reverted to the 49ers' practice squad Friday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Hodge played just one offensive snap in Thursday's 27-7 victory over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia. The wide receiver played 12 more snaps on special teams, where he recorded two tackles on kick coverage. The 31-year-old veteran player will likely see more action throughout the season as a special teams option for the 49ers.

items.headline: James (coach's decision) is officially inactive for Thursday's game against the Rams, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.summary: The 2025 fifth-rounder will not suit up in Week 1, leaving Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black as the only healthy running backs active for the 49ers on Thursday. James' role moving forward may depend on how effective Black is to start the season.

items.headline: Purdy completed 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding five rushes for 29 yards during the 49ers' 27-7 Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
items.summary: After an offseason in which the Rams' fearsome pass rush garnered plenty of headlines, Purdy navigated the season-opening matchup against his talented NFC West rival in nearly flawless fashion. The fifth-year signal-caller got off to a fast start with new No. 1 receiver Mike Evans, connecting with him on three occasions for 22 yards during a 15-play opening drive that culminated in a field goal. Purdy went on to hit Evans for a contested two-yard scoring strike early in the third quarter, and he sandwiched impressive touchdown tosses to Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel of 39 and 15 yards, respectively, around that play. Purdy's early second-quarter interception on a pass intended for George Kittle did lead to the Rams' only touchdown, but as the final numbers indicate, the veteran quarterback did more than enough to atone. Purdy should have a strong chance of carrying over the season-opening momentum into Week 2, as a home date with what's expected to be a vulnerable Dolphins defense awaits on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.headline: Robinson caught two passes (on three targets) for 50 yards and a touchdown during the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams in Week 1.
items.summary: Robinson snuck past the Rams secondary midway through the second quarter to haul in a 39-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy and give the 49ers a 10-7 lead, with the former adding an 11-yard grab early in the third frame that led to a Mike Evans two-yard touchdown catch three plays later. Robinson played 41 of the 49ers' 65 snaps on offense (63.1 percent), which was second-most among San Francisco wideouts behind Evans (49) and ahead of Deebo Samuel (27). Robinson's extended snap count was largely due to rookie second-rounder De'Zhaun Stribling suffering an ankle injury in the first quarter, and the former could operate in an elevated role in Week 2 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Sept. 20 if Stribling is unable to play.

items.headline: Rourke (ribs) did not appear on the 49ers' injury report Tuesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.summary: Rourke has fully recovered from the ribs injury that he suffered during the preseason. He will now be good to go for Thursday night's regular-season opener against the Rams in Australia.

items.headline: Coach Kyle Shanahan said after Thursday night's win over the Rams that Tonges' knee injury "does not look good," Vic Tafur of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Tonges hobbled off with the assistance of trainers in the second quarter against Los Angeles and was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the contest. He now appears to be looking at an extended absence. Luke Farrell soaked up the TE2 snaps behind George Kittle following Tonges' departure.

items.headline: Watkins (coach's decision) is officially inactive for Thursday's game against the Rams, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.summary: After flashing during the preseason, Watkins will be a healthy scratch to begin the regular season. Presumably, veterans Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel and rookie second-rounder De'Zhaun Stribling will see the lion's share of the 49ers' snaps at wide receiver in Week 1.

items.headline: The 49ers signed Dinkins to the practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: The 49ers waived Dinkins during Sunday's cut-down day. The tight end cleared waivers and has rejoined the 49ers, who signed him to a three-year contract on Aug. 22. Dinkins has a good chance to be elevated to the active roster if George Kittle (Achilles), Jake Tonges, Luke Farrell or Brayden Willis (concussion) miss time due to injury.

items.headline: The 49ers signed Grimes to the practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: The 49ers waived Grimes during Sunday's cut-down day. The undrafted free agent out of NC State had a strong enough postseason to be awarded an invite to the 49ers' practice squad. The wide receiver participated in the team's first preseason game against the Titans, catching his sole target for seven yards.

items.headline: The 49ers signed McCormick to the practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: The 49ers waived McCormick during Sunday's cut-down day. The running back had a strong preseason, rushing 23 times for 99 yards and a touchdown. The team invited the 25-year-old to the practice squad as soon as he cleared waivers.

items.headline: The 49ers signed Pauling to the practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: The 49ers waived Pauling during Sunday's cut-down day. The undrafted free agent out of Notre Dame cleared waivers and had a successful enough training camp to be invited to the practice squad. The wide receiver participated in all three preseason games, catching three of his five targets for eight yards.

items.headline: The 49ers signed Willis to the practice squad Sunday.
items.summary: The 49ers' seventh-round pick from 2023 will return to the team's practice squad shortly before the beginning of the regular season. Willis has played in 23 games for the 49ers, logging 85 offensive snaps and 358 special teams snaps.

items.headline: Arroyo wasn't targeted in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the Patriots.
items.summary: Arroyo was on the field for 11 of Seattle's 50 snaps on offense while AJ Barner played 44 snaps and caught two passes, suggesting there is still a substantial gap between the Seahawks' top two tight ends. After flashing some receiving upside during the preseason, it looks like Arroyo may not get enough playing time to make much of an impact on offense, at least while Barner is healthy.

items.headline: Barner caught both of his targets for 13 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the Patriots.
items.summary: Barner was on the field for 44 of Seattle's 50 snaps on offense, so he remains firmly entrenched atop the tight end depth chart. He also had a short rushing gain from under center erased by an offensive offside penalty. Barner tied for second on the team in catches, as the Seahawks didn't get much production in the passing game from anyone other than Jaxson Smith-Njigba (eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown) in a game that saw starting QB Sam Darnold (hip) exit in the first quarter. Darnold is expected to sit out Week 2 against the Cardinals, in which case Drew Lock would draw the start under center.

items.headline: Foster is among the five wide receivers that made Seattle's initial 53-man roster, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Foster earned his roster spot with a strong training camp that carried over into a productive preseason, which included a touchdown catch in Seattle's first preseason game. The 25-year-old wide receiver finished the previous season on Seattle's practice squad but has yet to appear in a regular-season game. Foster will likely be limited to a depth role barring injuries to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, Cooper Kupp or Tory Horton (undisclosed), the last of whom isn't believed to have a long-term injury.

items.headline: Holani rushed eight times for 29 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Seahawks' 13-10 win over the Patriots on Wednesday.
items.summary: The change-of-pace back ironically logged just two fewer carries than lead runner Jadarian Price while also being a complete non-factor as a pass catcher. Holani ran reasonably well against a tough Patriots front, and his carry total served as the second-highest tally of his career. Holani should continue to see 8-to-10 touches per game as a complementary option while Zach Charbonnet (knee) remains on the PUP list.

items.headline: Horton (hamstring) is inactive for Wednesday night's game against the Patriots.
items.summary: The 2025 fifth-rounder was not able to recover from his hamstring injury in time for the Seahawks' Week 1 contest. Montorie Foster will take over as the No. 4 wide receiver behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed and Cooper Kupp for the contest.

items.headline: Jones played 17 special-teams snaps during the Seahawks' 13-10 win versus the Patriots on Wednesday.
items.summary: Jones' only notable involvement in Week 1 came in the third quarter when he downed a punt at New England's six-yard line, setting up a three and out. The Seahawks will be able to elevate him twice more before they'd have to sign him to the active roster in order for him to suit up.

items.headline: Kupp caught two of three targets for 35 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the Patriots.
items.summary: Kupp turned the tide with a spectacular one-handed grab for 24 yards in the third quarter while the Seahawks trailed 10-0. He thought he had a seven-yard touchdown three plays later, but the scoring play was nullified by an illegal shift penalty. Seattle would settle for a field goal to kickstart a 13-0 run to end the game. Kupp finished a distant second in receiving yards behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 122, which could be a preview of the team's pecking order in the passing game all season. Sam Darnold (hip) exited in the first quarter of Wednesday's win, and Drew Lock is likely to be Seattle's starting QB in Week 2 against the Cardinals while Darnold's on the mend.

items.headline: Milroe (coach's decision) will be the emergency third quarterback for the Wednesday night matchup with the Patriots.
items.summary: Milroe is the No. 3 quarterback behind Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. The second-year player is already settling into what will likely be his weekly role throughout the 2026 season, set to only check in to the game if both quarterbacks are unable to continue playing.

items.headline: Shaheed caught one of three targets for four yards while adding three kickoff returns for 80 yards and a nine-yard punt return in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the Patriots.
items.summary: After some offseason whispers about a larger role on offense for Shaheed, that didn't materialize in the season opener, as he wasn't among the five players who recorded multiple catches for the Seahawks. The standout return man maintained his prominent role on special teams, and he was on the field for 33 of Seattle's 50 snaps on offense. Shaheed is likely to have Drew Lock as his quarterback Week 2 against the Cardinals, as starting signal-caller Sam Darnold (hip) is likely to miss that game after exiting in the first quarter Wednesday.

items.headline: Wilson rushed twice for three yards and wasn't targeted in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the Patriots.
items.summary: Wilson worked as a distant third option in Seattle's backfield behind Jadarian Price (58 yards on 12 touches) and George Holani (29 yards on eight touches). As long as Price and Holani are healthy, Wilson is unlikely to get meaningful playing time, and Seattle's backfield could get even more crowded once Zach Charbonnet (knee) comes off the PUP list.

items.headline: Coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Charbonnet (knee) looks "awesome" in his rehab from a torn ACL, Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports.
items.summary: Macdonald added that Charbonnet looks "dang good." The running back is on reserve/PUP to begin the season and will miss at least the first four games, but it sounds like he could return sometime next month. Seattle's backfield picture remains murky with rookie Jadarian Price, George Holani and Emanuel Wilson all options to see snaps. Adding Charbonnet's name to the mix will only muddy the picture. Price looks like the best bet for fantasy production, but the coaching staff has an affinity for Charbonnet, especially near the goal line.

items.headline: The Seahawks signed Henderson to the practice squad Monday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Seahawks waived Henderson on Sunday, and the rookie sixth-round pick out of Kansas was surprisingly able to clear waivers and has once again signed with the Super Bowl champs. Henderson had a strong preseason, catching four of his six targets for 65 yards and adding 88 return yards on four returns over three games.

items.headline: The Seahawks signed Hicks to the practice squad Monday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hicks cleared waivers after being waived by the Seahawks during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver has been waived twice by the team this August but keeps finding his way back to the organization. Hicks participated in the final two preseason games for the Seahawks, catching his sole target for 12 yards.

items.headline: The Seahawks signed White to the practice squad Monday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Seahawks waived White during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and will once again become a member of the team's practice squad. White spent the 2025 season on the practice squad and was elevated to the active roster for two regular-season games. The 24-year-old participated in 22 total snaps and will likely see a similar number of chances in 2026.

items.headline: The Seahawks signed Wright to the practice squad Monday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Seahawks waived Wright on Sunday, however, the running back showed enough value in training camp to receive an invitation to the team's practice squad once he cleared waivers. Wright played in the last two preseason contests for the Seahawks, rushing 23 times for 114 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: Godwin caught all four of his targets for 40 yards in the Bucs' 33-27 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. He added three rushing yards on one carry.
items.summary: Godwin's 32 routes on Baker Mayfield's 36 dropbacks were second on the team behind Emeka Egbuka, who ran 33 routes, and Godwin was lined up in the slot 54.3 percent of the time, while Egbuka and Ted Hurst mainly played on the outside. Godwin was targeted just four times, however, finishing fourth on the team. Now 30 years old with multiple serious lower-body injuries in his career, it's fair to wonder how much explosiveness Godwin has left. He's a low-floor WR3/4 in fantasy ahead of next Sunday's date with the Browns.

items.headline: Hurst caught all three of his targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 33-27 loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: With Jalen McMillan (knee) inactive, Hurst played 75 percent of the offensive snaps against Cincinnati and ran 30 routes on Baker Mayfield's 36 dropbacks. Hurst's three targets were fifth on the team. McMillan's injury isn't expected to keep him out long, so Hurst will be competing for playing time once everyone is healthy. Hurst is merely someone to watch on the waiver wire in normal-sized redraft fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 2
items.summary: Will the Titans score any points against the Eagles? Can Ben Johnson solve Brian Flores' Vikings defense? Get ready for Week 2 with seven takes.

items.headline: Otton caught three of five targets for 26 yards in Tampa Bay's loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
items.summary: Otton played 56 of 57 offensive snaps and ran 31 routes on Baker Mayfield's 36 dropbacks. His five targets were good for third on the team, trailing only Bucky Irving's seven and Emeka Egbuka's six. Otton plays virtually every snap, but he's a low-floor, low-upside fantasy option who caught just one touchdown last season.

items.headline: Tucker (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game at Cincinnati, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
items.summary: Tucker followed up a DNP on Wednesday due to a hamstring injury with limited sessions both Thursday and Friday before the Buccaneers listed him as doubtful for Week 1 action. Now that Tucker will be in street clothes Sunday, Josh Williams will be the sole active running back behind the team's top duo of Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell. Tucker's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Sept. 20 versus the Browns.

items.headline: Williams reverted to the Buccaneers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Williams saw five special teams snaps in Sunday's 33-27 loss to the Bengals. The running back returned one kick for 47 yards. Williams' one explosive play may be enough to merit another elevation if the Buccaneers still require depth at returner for the Week 2 game against the Browns.

items.headline: Dippre agreed to sign with the Buccaneers' practice squad Tuesday, Jenna Laine of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: After going undrafted out of Alabama in 2025, Dippre was able to secure a spot on the Patriots' roster coming out of his first training camp but was limited to just two appearances during the regular season. The 24-year-old couldn't make the cut following his second camp with New England but was able to quickly find a new opportunity in Tampa Bay.

items.headline: The Buccaneers signed Greene to the practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Buccaneers waived Green during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver spent the entire 2025 season on the practice squad and promptly returned to the unit once he cleared Sunday's waivers. Greene was not elevated for a game during the 2025 season, but his six receptions for 80 yards over three preseason games in 2026 show he may have improved enough to suit up a few times throughout the regular season.

items.headline: The Buccaneers signed Patterson to the practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Buccaneers waived Patterson during Sunday's cutdown day. The undrafted free agent out of Georgia Tech cleared waivers and promptly re-signed with the team that took a shot on him in late May. Patterson participated in all three preseason games, catching 13 passes for 72 yards.

items.headline: The Buccaneers signed Rivers to the practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Buccaneers waived Rivers during Sunday's cut-down day. The undrafted free agent out of Georgia Tech was productive enough throughout training camp to be invited to the Buccaneers' practice squad after clearing waivers. Rivers had a solid preseason, catching eight passes for 41 yards and rushing once for seven yards. The wide receiver may yet get a chance to show off his 4.35-second speed at some point during the regular season if he is elevated to the active roster.

items.headline: The Buccaneers signed Stick to the practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Colts released Stick on Sunday, but the quarterback has found a new home with the Buccaneers and will provide additional depth in case Baker Mayfield or Jalon Daniels miss time during the 2026 season.

items.headline: Ayomanor caught one of three targets for an 11-yard touchdown in the Titans' 23-10 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
items.summary: Ayomanor played as the Titans' WR4, seeing 26 snaps behind Carnell Tate (44), Wan'Dale Robinson (41) and Calvin Ridley (32). It was Ayomanor who accounted for the team's lone touchdown, but he's going to need an injury or two ahead of him to have any chance at fantasy viability in a Tennessee passing offense that is in the conversation as the worst in the league.

items.headline: Bellinger caught his sole target for seven yards in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the Jets.
items.summary: Bellinger is the second option at tight end behind Gunner Helm and was used like it. The 25-year-old played just 14 of the Titans' 50 offensive snaps and was also only used for three special teams snaps over the course of the night.

items.headline: Dike recorded one catch for seven yards, three kick returns for 62 yards and one punt return for -5 yards in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the Jets.
items.summary: The wide receiver only saw four snaps on offense behind Carnell Tate (43 snaps), Wan'Dale Robinson (40), Calvin Ridley (31) and Elic Ayomanor (26), though he did see nine special-teams snaps. Dike also lost a fumble on one of his kickoff returns. The second-year pro is not even really a streamable fantasy asset if he's going to remain buried on the wide receiver depth chart.

items.headline: Helm caught four of five targets for 28 yards in the Titans' 23-10 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
items.summary: Helm's five targets trailed both Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson, as the duo drew six targets apiece to lead the team in Week 1. Even more importantly for Helm's fantasy prospects, he ran 22 routes to Daniel Bellinger's five, suggesting he's well ahead of Bellinger on the depth chart as a pass catcher. Helm will be a lower-end TE2 next Sunday against the Eagles.

items.headline: Ridley played 32 offensive snaps and did not show up in the box score otherwise during the Titans' 23-10 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
items.summary: Ridley had the third-most snaps among Titans wide receivers behind Carnell Tate (44) and Wan'Dale Robinson (41), though Ridley didn't end up seeing a single target from quarterback Cam Ward during Sunday's loss. Ridley restructured his contract in mid-March after playing in only seven regular-season games in 2025, but it looks like the veteran wide receiver might be an afterthought in the Titans' offense. He'll look for better results in Tennessee's Week 2 clash against Philadelphia on Sept. 20.

items.headline: Robinson finished Sunday's Week 1 loss to the Jets with five catches for 38 yards.
items.summary: Tennessee's offense struggled as a whole Sunday, and the addition of Robinson and rookie Carnell Tate to the wideout corps didn't do much to improve QB Cam Ward's performance following a disappointing rookie season. Robinson and Tate both turned six targets into 38 yards, with Robinson logging five catches to Tate's four. As has been the case throughout Robinson's career, he was deployed mostly in short yardage, averaging a meager 7.6 yards per catch. Robinson blossomed with the Giants last year for a career-best 1,014 receiving yards on 92 catches, but he may struggle to reach those marks in 2026 if Ward doesn't show considerable improvement.

items.headline: Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.summary: The rookie fifth-rounder will be a healthy scratch Week 1 while the Titans role with three active running backs in Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears and Julius Chestnut. Singleton's next opportunity to make his NFL regular-season debut is Week 2 against the Eagles on Sunday, Sept. 20, though he's unlikely to suit up for that contest unless one of Pollard, Spears or Chestnut is sidelined.

items.headline: Spears rushed three times for 12 yards and caught two of four targets for an additional 12 yards in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the Jets.
items.summary: Tony Pollard narrowly out-snapped Spears, 26-25, in the season opener, as the former out-carried Spears seven to three in what was a decidedly negative game script for the Titans. Spears out-targeted his backfield mate four to two and ran 14 routes to Pollard's seven. This looks like a pretty even split, but it'll be tough for either back to produce weekly fantasy reliability in one of the league's worst offenses with a swinging-gate offensive line.

items.headline: Trubisky (biceps) was not listed on the Titans' injury report Wednesday.
items.summary: Trubisky was dealing with a biceps injury over the last couple of weeks of training camp, but his absence from Wednesday's injury report indicates he'll suit up for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Jets. With Will Levis no longer on the roster, Trubisky will serve as Cam Ward's backup, with Hendon Hooker on the Titans' practice squad.

items.headline: The Titans signed Carter to the practice squad Monday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Carter was released by the Titans on Sunday, but he was back with the organization 24 hours later. The 2021 fourth-round pick of the Jets has appeared in 61 regular-season games with New York and the Cardinals, amassing 1,692 rushing yards off 418 attempts and catching 145 passes for 1,038 yards while totaling 10 total touchdowns (nine rushing, one receiving). Carter has a fair amount of starting experience and put together some serviceable performances for Arizona down the stretch last season, so he could get a chance to see the field for the Titans at some point during the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: The Titans signed Hooker to the practice squad Monday, Jim Wyatt of the Team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hooker was waived by Tennessee on Sunday but will stay with the team in some capacity as a member of the practice squad. The 28-year-old was selected by the Lions in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He appeared in three regular-season games for Detroit in 2024, going 6-for-9 for 6 yards and adding five carries for two yards. While Hooker could suit up for the Titans during the 2026 campaign, he is a long way away from earning a starting opportunity.

items.headline: The Titans signed Montgomery to its practice squad Monday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.summary: Montgomery totaled two catches for 25 over his three preseason games, which helped to earn him a place on the Titans' practice squad to start the new campaign. He was productive with an age advantage at John Carroll, but it may take injuries for him to be elevated to Tennessee's active roster in 2026.

items.headline: Tennessee signed Mullings (hip) to its practice squad Monday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.summary: Mullings was sidelined during the preseason due to a hip injury, but he's apparently in good enough shape to contribute as a member of Tennessee's practice squad. In nine games with the team in 2025, he totaled three carries for seven yards.

items.headline: Tennessee signed Osborn to the practice squad Monday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: After being released by Tennessee on Sunday, Osborn will join the Titans' practice squad. The 29-year-old has plenty of NFL experience, suiting up for the Vikings and Patriots throughout his career. In 66 regular-season games, he recorded 165 catches for 1,902 yards and 16 touchdowns. Osborn could find his way to the field during the 2026 campaign, though he's not expected to be much of a contributor if he does.

items.headline: Tennessee signed Restrepo to its practice squad Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.summary: Restrepo made Tennessee's initial 53-man roster for 2026, but he was abruptly waived Monday to make room for new acquisitions. Now he's back with the organization as a member of the practice squad, and since the Titans only have five receivers on their active roster, he might be closer to the field than most practice-squad wideouts.

items.headline: Tennessee signed Wilson to its practice squad Monday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.summary: Wilson was waived Sunday after missing the cut for Tennessee's initial 53-man roster, but he's now back with the team. He's been bouncing around the league since 2023, but he's still waiting to make his regular-season debut.

items.headline: Allen turned four carries into 16 yards during the Commanders' 24-22 loss to the Eagles on Sunday.
items.summary: Allen didn't record his first NFL carry until the third quarter, though he did log three rushes for 11 yards during the Commanders' final offensive drive of the game. The rookie sixth-rounder played only seven snaps on offense, well behind fellow running backs Jacory Croskey-Merritt (34) and Rachaad White (29). Allen figures to see limited work out of the Commanders' backfield this season unless one or both of Croskey-Merrit and White were to miss time. Washington has another NFC East matchup on tap, a Week 2 road tilt against Dallas on Sept. 20.

items.headline: Bates caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Eagles.
items.summary: Bates started along with Chig Okonkwo at tight end, and he garnered more than two targets in a regular-season game for the first time since Week 9 of the 2025 campaign. Bates was on the field for 34 of the team's 70 total offensive snaps while also logging 15 more snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Brown failed to haul in either of his two targets during the Commanders' 24-22 loss to the Eagles on Sunday.
items.summary: Brown played 37 of 70 offensive snaps (52.9 percent), which was third-most among Commanders wide receivers behind Terry McLaurin (61) and Stefon Diggs (44). However, Brown was unable reel in the two passes he saw from Jayden Daniels, whereas rookie third-rounder Antonio Williams finished with a 4-66-1 receiving line despite playing only 26 offensive snaps. Brown will look for better results in Washington's Week 2 clash against Dallas on Sept. 20.

items.headline: Burks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
items.summary: Burks appeared in eight of the Commanders' final nine games of the 2025 regular season after being released by the Titans in October. However, the 2022 first-rounder will join Luke McCaffrey (coach's decision) in street clothes Sunday, with the Commanders opting for five active wide receivers for game day. Burks' next chance to play is Week 2 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.headline: Kaliakmanis (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Commanders' emergency third quarterback against the Eagles on Sunday.
items.summary: As the emergency third quarterback, Kaliakmanis is prohibited from playing in Sunday's game unless both Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota were to leave the contest due to injury, illness or ejection. Kaliakmanis was a seventh-round selection of the Commanders in the 2026 NFL Draft after spending the last two years of his college career at Rutgers.

items.headline: Lane caught his only target for four yards while returning four punts for 53 yards and three kicks for 95 yards in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Eagles.
items.summary: Lane played 18 offensive snaps and 12 special teams snaps in the contest. The primary kick and punt returner amassed 148 total return yards, providing strong field position as the Commanders battled a divisional rival.

items.headline: Mariota (knee) practiced in full Wednesday.
items.summary: Mariota suffered a sprained MCL during the preseason, though it appears the injury is behind him heading into the Week 1 opener versus Philadelphia. The 32-year-old appeared in 11 regular-season games for the Commanders in 2025, throwing for 1,695 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions off 139-for-227 passing, adding 50 carries for 297 yards and one touchdown. Mariota currently sits at the No. 2 spot on the depth chart behind Jayden Daniels.

items.headline: McCaffrey (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
items.summary: McCaffrey, a third-round selection of the Commanders in 2024 NFL Draft, appeared in 26 regular-season games over the first two years of his NFL career. However, he'll be a healthy scratch for Sunday's regular-season opener, with the Commanders carrying five active wide receivers for Week 1. McCaffrey's next chance to play is Week 2 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.headline: McLaurin caught two of four targets for 14 yards against Philadelphia in a loss Sunday.
items.summary: McLaurin surprisingly took a back seat to third-round rookie Antonio Williams (4-61-1) and veteran Stefon Diggs (4-55-1) in the season opener. McLaurin had as many targets (four) as Williams but logged less than half as many as Diggs' nine. It's expected that McLaurin will serve as the Commanders' No. 1 wideout again this year, but with Diggs and Williams both new to the receiving corps, it remains to be seen how QB Jayden Daniels will adjust his distribution of targets. McLaurin will look for a more robust line in Week 2, when Washington will face the Cowboys, who gave up the most passing yards in the league last year.

items.headline: Okonkwo is questionable to return to Sunday's Week 1 game against Philadelphia due to a hamstring injury.
items.summary: Okonkwo was deemed questionable to return in the second half of a close contest. Before exiting, he had caught two of three targets for 16 yards. If Okonkwo can't return to the Week 1 matchup, John Bates and Ben Sinnott figure to handle Washington's tight-end snaps.

items.headline: Sinnott played on 18 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams snaps but did not record a stat in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Eagles.
items.summary: The tight end was third in his positional rotation behind Chig Okonkwo (38 snaps) and John Bates (32). Sinnott caught 16 passes across his first two regular seasons in the NFL, but he has functioned mainly as a blocker in his professional career.

items.headline: White rushed seven times for 22 yards and caught two of three targets for five yards in Sunday's loss to Dallas in Week 1.
items.summary: White had a long run of nine yards but was held to 13 yards across his other six carries. He did see a substantial amount of action, logging 27 offensive snaps to Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 33, with Kaytron Allen mixing in for six snaps. White was the only one of the trio to gain positive yards through the air, and he's likely to feature as the Commanders' top pass-catching back in 2026 while mostly deferring to Croskey-Merritt on the ground.

items.headline: Williams hauled in all four of his targets for 64 yards and a touchdown during the Commanders' 24-22 loss to the Eagles on Sunday.
items.summary: Williams played only 26 of 70 offensive snaps (37.1 percent), which was fourth-most among Commanders wide receivers in Sunday's loss. However, the rookie third-rounder ended up leading the Commanders in receiving yards while finishing second behind veteran Stefon Diggs in targets (nine). Williams was close to scoring on his first NFL catch for 16 yards late in the second quarter, falling short of the goal line before Jacory Croskey-Merritt punched the ball in on a one-yard rushing touchdown on the next play. Williams followed that up with a 33-yard catch early in the fourth quarter before hauling in a one-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels late in the frame. It was an encouraging NFL debut from Williams, who may have benefited from the Eagles' secondary focusing on limiting Terry McLaurin, though the former may have shown enough against Philadelphia to warrant additional playing time moving forward. The Commanders will stay on the road for their Week 2 clash against the Cowboys on Sept. 20.

items.headline: Washington signed Bradley to its practice squad Monday, Zach Selby of the Commanders' official site reports.
items.summary: Bradley was waived Sunday after missing the cut for Washington's initial 53-man roster, but he's now back with the organization as a member of the practice squad. His length gives him the ability to potentially line up outside the numbers if he's elevated to the active roster in 2026.

items.headline: The Commanders signed Hartman to the practice squad Monday, Zach Selby of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hartman went undrafted in 2024, and while he has remained affiliated with the Commanders since then, he has mostly been relegated to the practice squad. There's a chance the 27-year-old could be elevated during the 2026 campaign, though he still likely wouldn't see any action.

items.headline: Washington signed Henry to its practice squad Monday, Zach Selby of the Commanders' official site reports.
items.summary: Henry had a decently productive preseason as a rusher (26 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown), but it wasn't enough to earn him a spot on the Commanders' initial 53-man roster, and now he'll start the new campaign on the practice squad. If free-agent acquisition Rachaad White (hamstring) is unable to play in Week 1, Henry could find himself on the short list for elevations to the active roster.

items.headline: Jefferson signed with the Commanders' practice squad Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: The wide receiver was released by Washington on Aug. 30. Jefferson has 166 career regular-season catches for 2,226 yards and 13 touchdowns across six different NFL campaigns. In Washington, he joins a receiver room that thins out significantly after veterans Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs.

items.headline: The Commanders signed Reynolds to the practice squad Monday, Zach Selby of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Reynolds was released by the Commanders on Sunday but at least earned a spot on the practice squad. The 30-year-old has appeared in 57 regular-season games for the Commanders, Jaguars and Lions throughout his career in a complementary role, rushing for 658 yards and one touchdown off 154 attempts while adding 25 catches for 258 yards. Reynolds could be elevated at some point during the 2026 season, though that move would likely be only for depth purposes.

items.headline: Washington signed Westover to its practice squad Tuesday, Zach Selby of the Commanders' official site reports.
items.summary: Westover went unclaimed after the Patriots waived him Sunday, but now he's getting another shot with a new club. He suited up for 17 regular-season games with New England in 2025, catching one of his two total targets for no gain.
